rules.surface_condition: cut that splits a numeral from its measurement/unit word (NUM on one side, unit on the other)
rules.blamed_rule: cuts adjacent to numerals/dates often score high
rules.proposed_rule: If left_last is NUM and right_first is a measurement/unit token (or vice versa), reduce the score into a lower band (e.g. target band 0–40) so numeric+unit expressions are not spuriously ranked highest when they are split across the cut.

rules.surface_condition: cut that separates a named entity from a parenthetical identifier/acronym (the parenthetical starts the following token)
rules.proposed_rule: If the token immediately after the marker is a parenthetical identifier / short acronym (e.g. 'isil', 'kv62', 'nsa', 'minae'), lower the score into a medium/low band (e.g. target band 0–60) because splitting an entity from its parenthetical id often yields unreliable partial translations or contradiction.

rules.surface_condition: cut immediately before a sentence-starting pronoun / contraction (e.g. it / it's) that begins the next sentence
rules.proposed_rule: If the token immediately after the marker is a sentence-initial pronoun/contraction ('it', "it's"), raise the score (e.g. target band 60–100). Do this despite the generic downward bias for auxiliaries/pronouns, because cuts before an initial-sentence pronoun often produce high measured values in the data.

tie_fix: Ties appear when multiple surface-based biases cancel each other (e.g. a numeral and a downward-function-word bias). Break ties deterministically by preferring the earlier marker instead of emitting equal numbers.
summary: The model systematically over-ranks cuts that split numeric measurements (NUM vs unit) and some parenthetical identifiers: it treats numerals and short named tokens as inherently high-quality anchors even when splitting the quantity or name causes contradiction or fragmentation. It also under-ranks a small class of cuts that precede sentence-initial pronouns (it / it's) which the labels often mark as good. Adjust scoring to demote NUM–unit splits and parenthetical separations, and to lift cuts before initial-sentence pronouns.
